weather_line: Fog on the corridor · spur country ahead · ducks at ease

stories.headline: Ashworth's Sketch Arrives by Owl: The Spur Above Marker 9 Has a Shape Now, and the Shape Is Interesting
body: A rolled paper arrived before breakfast — no cover note, no seal — containing a rough sketch in the same burnt-sienna ink as the stamp on the orange duck. Mira Ashworth's hand is spare and exact: a single climbing line, northeast, with three hash marks indicating gradient, a notation that reads 'shelf?' at the hundred-yard limit, and a small circle above that with no label at all. The circle is either a clearing, a rock feature, or something Ashworth has not yet decided how to describe.

Steve unrolled it on the kitchen table beside the chart and weighted it with the flint stone. The spur's mouth, as sketched, aligns with a narrow gap in the treeline that he passed without stopping on yesterday morning's drive up the corridor — a shadow between two ridgelines, the kind the Jeep registers as a question. He went back after lunch. The gap is real. The ground beyond it is uneven, steeply angled, and covered in the particular shade of wet leaf-shadow that trails acquire when no one has run them in a long while.
Christine has noted the gradient marks and the unlabelled circle and said, precisely: 'That's not a question mark. That's an invitation.' The expedition file is open. Day 3 will establish a date.

stories.headline: Dispatch Received from Abroad: Andrew's Sunday Owl Contains No Actionable Intelligence, Remains Thoroughly Welcome
body: The Prophet's foreign correspondent — stationed, as readers will recall, at an undisclosed distance — filed his weekly dispatch overnight. The contents remain classified in the interest of sibling confidentiality, but sources confirm the owl arrived plump, punctual, and in good spirits, which is the correspondent's signature.

Andrew's dispatches are notable for their warmth-to-word-count ratio, which the Prophet's editorial board rates annually as the highest of any contributing bureau. This week's submission is no exception. He is, by all accounts, well. He asks about the dogs. He always asks about the dogs.

stories.headline: The Three Ducks Hold Formation; the Jeep Has Expressed No Opinion Since Thursday; Jersey Believes This Is Fine
body: The three ducks — original pale, orange Survey 7, green centre — have now been in their bonnet triangle for thirty-six hours without disturbance. The forty-seven-degree alignment between the outer two remains unchanged. Steve has checked the mirror angles twice, not because he suspects movement but because checking is how he demonstrates regard. The Jeep received this without comment.

Jersey, who spent most of Saturday in the warm spot between the sitting-room rug and the kitchen doorway, has assessed the duck situation and returned a formal verdict of 'fine.' He has no further questions at this time. The Ministry's subcommittee, reached for comment, noted it remains technically convened but accepted that Sunday is not a jurisdiction day.

stories.headline: Ministry's Weekend Circular Arrives; Acknowledges That the Spur Above Marker 9 Does Not Officially Exist; Notes This Has Not Historically Stopped Anyone
body: The Department of Magical Cartography issued its Sunday circular this morning, which contained — buried beneath fourteen paragraphs concerning flood-plain reclassification in the eastern vales — a single unremarked sentence: 'Survey Marker 9 (Harlan's Creek corridor) currently marks the upper extent of the charted region. Terrain above this point is logged as unsurveyed.' The circular then continued its business about flood plains.

A Ministry spokesperson confirmed that 'unsurveyed' is not the same as 'impassable,' 'prohibited,' or 'inadvisable,' and that the Department of Magical Cartography would be 'professionally interested' in any field annotations submitted by qualified parties. Christine read this once, set it down, and went to find her trail notes from the Keeps Ridge crossing. She is, by all available definitions, a qualified party.

familiars_corner: Lucy: Has reviewed Ashworth's sketch — specifically the unlabelled circle — and returned it to the table without touching the flint stone, which is either professional courtesy or a territorial claim; no one is certain which.

Ellie: Discovered this morning that the green duck on the bonnet also has a reflection in the Jeep's windscreen and spent a companionable quarter-hour sitting with it; the reflection did not explain the spur but seemed sympathetic.

Jersey: Successfully occupied three consecutive warm spots between six a.m. and noon, completing what experts are calling a masterclass in Sunday logistics; he is resting now, in preparation for the afternoon's resting.
founding_editor_note: That unlabelled circle on the sketch? I'd have put a nail there and worked backward. You almost always find out what a thing is by building toward it. — D.

in_brief.sport: Sunday Rest Report: Steve lifted nothing heavier than the flint stone and the rolled sketch; Christine considers this acceptable, provisionally.
in_brief.forecast: Fog persisting in the Harlan's Creek corridor through midweek; the spur's mouth remains visible; the circle above the shelf remains unlabelled and is not expected to label itself.

storyline_updates.title: Above Marker 9
storyline_updates.summary: Day 2: Ashworth's sketch arrived by owl — burnt-sienna ink, spare and exact. It shows the spur's climbing line with three gradient marks, a notation reading 'shelf?' at the hundred-yard limit, and an unlabelled circle above that. Steve confirmed the spur's mouth on a Sunday drive: a real gap in the treeline, uneven ground, long-unrun. Christine has identified the sketch as an invitation, not a question. The expedition file is open; Day 3 should establish a run date, perhaps a first attempt to drive the mouth or scout the shelf — or a second communication from Ashworth with more detail about the unlabelled circle, which neither Steve nor Christine has yet asked her about directly.
